<thought>We have the molecular ion at m/z ≈ 199 Da and a 13C NMR showing eight distinct carbon signals: four aromatic (138.8, 131.5 ×2, 130.6 ×2, 121.3 ppm) consistent with a para‑disubstituted benzene, plus two aliphatic signals (≈ 43.5 and 38.6 ppm) typical of benzylic CH₂ groups. To identify the exact structure we need the ¹H NMR data to see the proton pattern (aromatic multiplet, aliphatic signals, possible hetero‑atom‑bound protons). The next inexpensive experiment is to obtain the proton NMR spectrum.</thought>
